14 May 2026 · Paper · Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews 187, 106742

Integrated information and predictive processing theories of consciousness: an adversarial collaborative review (INTREPID)

Corcoran AW, Haun AM, Dorman R, Tononi G, Friston KJ, Pennartz CMA, TWCF INTREPID Consortium

The second big adversarial collaboration has published its plan: IIT against two predictive-brain theories. No results yet.

Three teams with rival theories wrote down, together, which experiments would tell their ideas apart and what each result would mean. The experiments run across several labs. This paper is the agreed plan and a comparison of the theories, not the results.

Compares IIT, neurorepresentationalism (Pennartz) and active inference (Friston): target phenomena, explanatory styles, methods. Lists key hypotheses for multi-site experiments and what would support or challenge each theory, and proposes formally combining results across experiments and replications into a quantitative measure of evidential support per theory. Preprint arXiv:2509.00555 (v1 Aug 2025, v3 May 2026). Online 14 May 2026, issue Aug 2026.

What we do with it

If its data appears after we seal our predictions, it is a clean prospective test. Its evidence-pooling idea is a model for our own log-score comparison of theories. Planned

Read the original. Source checked against the original.
